newsitem.title: USA: Smoke forces evacuation of U.S. theme park.
newsitem.headline: Smoke forces evacuation of U.S. theme park.

text.p: Hundreds of tourists were forced to leave one of Florida's best-known theme parks Wednesday after Sea World of Florida filled with thick smoke from a brush fire near Orlando's tourist district.
No injuries to people or animals in the park were reported, Nick Gollattscheck, a Sea World spokesman, said. No other theme parks were affected.

"Nobody was in any danger, the animals weren't in danger, there was no fire in the park. The park was going to be closing at 7 anyway and we made the decision to close two hours early so our guests could get on with their evening," he said.

The fire began at about 3 p.m. EST when a power company worker digging nearby hit a power line, causing it to ignite. The wind spread the blaze, said Orange County Fire Rescue Division spokesman Lt. LaRon Graham.
Firefighters were on the scene, and had contained the blaze and intended to keep fighting it through the night. "The fire is contained. Now we're basically fighting the hot spots," Graham said.
The theme park, owned by Anheuser-Busch will reopen Thursday morning.
Visitors were offered free tickets and refunds.
